inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(63,15) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. S11.VBS names this address swURFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged right-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(3) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sURFlipper = 34) unless the table calls NoUpperRightFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleRFlip as a number other than True. The constant does not follow the PinMAME column, and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(63,15) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 15 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 15: a host write to 15 is overwritten on the next update. F-14 physical lower and upper right flippers share cabinet-side control; retained S11.VBS drives public 82.

mechanisms.behavior: Drained ball closes outhole10. Coil1 transfers it into the four-position gravity trough; positions11(right/front feed),12(right center),13(left center),14(left) register occupancy. Coil2 feeds the right/front ball into the manual shooter lane sensed by16. Retained script initializes four balls with 11-14 active and advances balls by gravity; this does not mean coil 1 directly actuates a trough switch electrically. Releasing sensors follows actual ball movement. Outhole or feeder jams leave the corresponding occupancy unchanged. No factory kick speed or VPX delay is canonically prescribed.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball outhole, trough and manual shooter

mechanisms.behavior: One ball rests in the named eject/lock lane and closes switch 21; output 7 drives the spring-return eject mechanism back toward the playfield. This is ball occupancy feedback, not an electrically direct coil-to-switch relation. The launch-ramp branches feed the three sensed lanes; ROM rules decide whether to retain or eject a ball. Persistent occupancy after a kick indicates a failed release/jam.
mechanisms.label: Right Eject

mechanisms.behavior: One ball rests in the named eject/lock lane and closes switch 22; output 10 drives the spring-return eject mechanism back toward the playfield. This is ball occupancy feedback, not an electrically direct coil-to-switch relation. The launch-ramp branches feed the three sensed lanes; ROM rules decide whether to retain or eject a ball. Persistent occupancy after a kick indicates a failed release/jam.
mechanisms.label: Left Center Eject

mechanisms.behavior: One ball rests in the named eject/lock lane and closes switch 23; output 5 drives the spring-return eject mechanism back toward the playfield. This is ball occupancy feedback, not an electrically direct coil-to-switch relation. The launch-ramp branches feed the three sensed lanes; ROM rules decide whether to retain or eject a ball. Persistent occupancy after a kick indicates a failed release/jam.
mechanisms.label: Right Center Eject

mechanisms.behavior: A ball in the top-right cup closes24. Coil3 lifts it vertically into the overhead rear channel; it joins the shooter route downstream of switch 20 and does not traverse that shooter ramp-entry sensor. Cup24 opens as the ball leaves. Spring and armature return the plunger. No limit/home switch or motor is fitted; the table animation timer is not physical travel data.
mechanisms.label: Top-right ball popper and overhead launch ramp

mechanisms.behavior: Two spring-return coil/plunger/arm drives on shared chassisD-11352 select among three branches. Energized upper 21 intercepts first into upper sensor 32 then right-center eject23, regardless of22. With 21 released and 22 energized, middle sensor 31 leads to left-center eject22. Both released selects lower sensor 30 to right eject21. This truth table follows exact collision walls and connected ramps reconciled with the factory layout. Branch sensors detect balls, not gate positions; no gate home/limit sensors are in the matrix. Apply the binding bulletin: adequate plunger insertion at rest, gates flush at the trough ports, corrected stop/washer.
mechanisms.label: Two launch-ramp diverter gates and three wire-ramp branches

mechanisms.behavior: The upper-left lane sensor 55 closes for a ball arriving in the Line-of-Death lane. Coil12 enables the kickback that returns it rapidly toward the lower playfield. Script ball-kicker and trigger are separate objects; collision timing and kick strength are table tuning, not a new sensor. The spring-return mechanism rests retracted.
mechanisms.label: Line-of-Death/Yagov kickback

mechanisms.behavior: Ball entering the left outlane closes61. The ROM drives13 when Rescue is available, returning the ball upfield; otherwise it drains. Spring return leaves the kicker retracted when inactive. A lane trigger is not an electrically direct coil sensor.
mechanisms.label: Left-outlane Rescue kickback

mechanisms.behavior: The physical scoring switch 57 registers the ball and the switch-driven special-solenoid slot fires17 only while game-on23 enables it; the ROM can also command the PIA special line. Actuating and scoring contacts are distinct where the assembly fits them. Mechanical spring return; no motor/home sensing.
mechanisms.label: Left slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: The physical scoring switch 58 registers the ball and the switch-driven special-solenoid slot fires18 only while game-on23 enables it; the ROM can also command the PIA special line. Actuating and scoring contacts are distinct where the assembly fits them. Mechanical spring return; no motor/home sensing.
mechanisms.label: Right slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: The physical scoring switch 28 registers the ball and the switch-driven special-solenoid slot fires20 only while game-on23 enables it; the ROM can also command the PIA special line. Actuating and scoring contacts are distinct where the assembly fits them. Mechanical spring return; no motor/home sensing.
mechanisms.label: Jet bumper

mechanisms.behavior: One 14-7946 motor and 20-9543 belt drive three reflector shafts under red/white/blue beacon domes; assembly bulbs are #1683/28V. Output16 controls the assembly. No home, index or travel sensor is documented; shutdown stops at the reached angle, and startup does not require a fabricated home state. Aircraft wings/flames in VPW are virtual additions.
mechanisms.label: Three rotating backbox-top beacons

mechanisms.behavior: Two lower FL11630 coils and two upper FL11722 coils are cabinet wired through their buttons and power-winding EOS contacts. Upper coils were revised by SS41. PinMAME sees buttons82 right/84 left and copies them to15/63;45/46 and 47/48 are synthetic paired enable states, not separate physical winding telemetry. The upper callback constants34/36 have no normal F-14 binary public output. Recreate physical upper/lower motion and staged cabinet control without inventing four independent CPU coil drivers.
mechanisms.label: Four cabinet-wired flippers

Physical relay11 energizes to open the normally closed GI supply contacts (full schematic PDF 10 K1). Binary output is raw relay state; VPW physical-output mode consumes integrated inverse bulb brightness. No separate GI0 channel exists. The table GI collection includes render helpers and six matrix bulbs for ambient shading, so neither collection count is a physical socket count. Exact complete GI quantity and string-member placement remain unproved. Observed individual modelled GI bulb envelope; a subset, not a complete hardware socket census. No helper count is promoted to quantity.

Factory printed circuit 12; exact wiring and complete original quantities are retained in manual-tables.md. Disclosed assembly projection: the coil is below the named kicker, bumper or slingshot; this is a physical mechanism anchor, not a measured winding center.

Factory printed circuit 13; exact wiring and complete original quantities are retained in manual-tables.md. Disclosed assembly projection: the coil is below the named kicker, bumper or slingshot; this is a physical mechanism anchor, not a measured winding center.

Factory printed circuit 14; exact wiring and complete original quantities are retained in manual-tables.md. Selects C-side25-32 when energized and A-side1-8 when released; it is not output 24. No relay-board origin is placed on the playfield.

Factory printed circuit 15; exact wiring and complete original quantities are retained in manual-tables.md. Population depends on factory/service state. Printed pre-SS41: 2 backbox + 1 RED2 playfield bulb; SS41 removes RED2 and preserves the backbox branch. Observed socket/dome of the retained pre-SS41 four-dome geometry. The post-update circuit population differs as disclosed; no backbox bulb is projected here.

Factory printed circuit 16; exact wiring and complete original quantities are retained in manual-tables.md. One 14-7946 belt motor turns three rotating reflectors; #1683 bulbs share the assembly control. No home/mark switch. Table aircraft wings/flames are virtual additions.

Parts page prints AE-26-1500-02 where the solenoid table prints AL-26-1500-02. Physical gate-arm world-mesh bounds provide an observed assembly projection; no off-playfield animation pivot is used.
